evidence_timeline.summary: We present NOT/ALFOSC optical spectroscopy of AT 2026aetp, an X-ray transient discovered by Einstein Probe on 2026-10-06 (see 'Body' for further details) and classified as a tidal disruption event (TDE). At the reported redshift of z = 0.1853, our spectrum obtained on 2026-10-08 shows a blue, featureless continuum, with a tentative broad, shallow emission feature consistent with He II λ4686. A Gaussian fit yields a high velocity of ~2.8 × 10⁴ km s⁻¹, although blending with other emission lines commonly observed in TDEs cannot be excluded. This tentative detection, together with the transient's blue optical colours, absolute magnitude (M ≈ −21.4 mag), X-ray emission, and nuclear location, further strengthens the case for its classification as a TDE.
evidence_timeline.title: Strengthening the case for classifying AT2026aetp as a TDE

publication_revisions.abstract: We present NOT/ALFOSC optical spectroscopy of AT 2026aetp, an X-ray transient discovered by Einstein Probe on 2026-10-06 (see 'Body' for further details) and classified as a tidal disruption event (TDE). At the reported redshift of z = 0.1853, our spectrum obtained on 2026-10-08 shows a blue, featureless continuum, with a tentative broad, shallow emission feature consistent with He II λ4686. A Gaussian fit yields a high velocity of ~2.8 × 10⁴ km s⁻¹, although blending with other emission lines commonly observed in TDEs cannot be excluded. This tentative detection, together with the transient's blue optical colours, absolute magnitude (M ≈ −21.4 mag), X-ray emission, and nuclear location, further strengthens the case for its classification as a TDE.
publication_revisions.title: Strengthening the case for classifying AT2026aetp as a TDE

publications.abstract: We present NOT/ALFOSC optical spectroscopy of AT 2026aetp, an X-ray transient discovered by Einstein Probe on 2026-10-06 (see 'Body' for further details) and classified as a tidal disruption event (TDE). At the reported redshift of z = 0.1853, our spectrum obtained on 2026-10-08 shows a blue, featureless continuum, with a tentative broad, shallow emission feature consistent with He II λ4686. A Gaussian fit yields a high velocity of ~2.8 × 10⁴ km s⁻¹, although blending with other emission lines commonly observed in TDEs cannot be excluded. This tentative detection, together with the transient's blue optical colours, absolute magnitude (M ≈ −21.4 mag), X-ray emission, and nuclear location, further strengthens the case for its classification as a TDE.
publications.title: Strengthening the case for classifying AT2026aetp as a TDE

publications.abstract: EP261006a (AT 2026aetp, Gaia DR3 2587044864659595392) was first detected by the Einstein Probe at 2026-10-06T17:49:57 UTC ([GCN #45826](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45826)) and was subsequently suggested to be a possible TDE ([GCN #45831](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45831)). Subsequent spectroscopic observations revealed a clear blue continuum across the entire spectrum, with no prominent absorption or emission features ([GCN #45833](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261006a#gcn-circular-45833)).
